title: Spinal Cord Microcircuit Atlas — Laminae, Columns, Tracts and Segmental Loops
purpose: Fill the biological interior of the Ladder. Separate vertebral rooms from the spinal cord's own gray-matter laminae, motor columns, autonomic columns, ascending tracts, descending tracts, local reflex circuits and central-pattern networks.
epistemic_rule: Spinal-cord organization is segmented neural tissue, not a chakra ladder. Project mappings are relational comparisons only.

gray_matter_rooms.name: Rexed I — Marginal Layer
roles: projection neurons receiving small-diameter afferent input
gray_matter_rooms.boundary: Pain is distributed; lamina I is not a pain center.

gray_matter_rooms.name: Rexed II — Substantia Gelatinosa
roles: modulation of nociceptive and somatosensory input
gray_matter_rooms.boundary: Gate-control metaphors are useful but simplified.

gray_matter_rooms.name: Rexed III–IV — Nucleus Proprius
gray_matter_rooms.boundary: Inputs and cell classes overlap laminar borders.

gray_matter_rooms.name: Rexed VII — Intermediate Zone
gray_matter_rooms.boundary: Very heterogeneous; not one functional center.

gray_matter_rooms.name: Clarke's Column
gray_matter_rooms.location: medial lamina VII, roughly C8/T1–L2/L3 segments
roles: unconscious proprioceptive relay to cerebellum via dorsal spinocerebellar tract

gray_matter_rooms.name: Sacral Parasympathetic Nucleus
gray_matter_rooms.boundary: Pelvic autonomic control is distributed with peripheral ganglia/plexuses.

gray_matter_rooms.name: Rexed IX — Motor Neuron Pools
roles: alpha/gamma motor neurons controlling skeletal muscle
gray_matter_rooms.boundary: Motor pools are muscle-specific and somatotopically organized.

gray_matter_rooms.name: Rexed X — Central Canal Commissural Room
gray_matter_rooms.boundary: Adult central canal patency is variable and often reduced.

white_matter_roads.name: Dorsal Columns
white_matter_roads.route: primary afferents ascend ipsilaterally to gracile/cuneate nuclei

white_matter_roads.name: Anterolateral System
white_matter_roads.route: spinal projection neurons cross and ascend toward brainstem/thalamic targets
roles: crude touch and related affective/arousal dimensions

white_matter_roads.name: Corticospinal Tract
white_matter_roads.route: motor cortex → brainstem → spinal interneurons/motor pools

white_matter_roads.name: Rubrospinal Neighbor
white_matter_roads.route: red nucleus → spinal cord, relatively reduced role in humans
white_matter_roads.boundary: Less dominant in humans than many nonhuman mammals.

segmental_loops.name: Stretch Reflex Loop
segmental_loops.route: muscle spindle Ia afferent → spinal circuitry → alpha motor neuron
segmental_loops.project: local correction without waiting for cortex

segmental_loops.name: Withdrawal / Flexor Reflex
segmental_loops.route: nociceptive input → interneuronal network → coordinated flexor/extensor response

segmental_loops.name: Crossed-Extensor Loop
segmental_loops.route: interneurons cross midline to stabilize opposite limb

segmental_loops.name: Locomotor Central-Pattern Networks
segmental_loops.route: distributed spinal interneuronal networks modulated by brainstem/sensory feedback
segmental_loops.boundary: Human locomotor circuitry is distributed and less directly accessible experimentally than animal models.

important_truths: The spinal cord itself has layered gray-matter rooms that do not correspond one-to-one with vertebrae.
A single vertebral room can contain cord segments with different segment names, especially inferiorly.
The cord is not only a cable: substantial preprocessing, gating, reflex control, autonomic output and rhythmic coordination occur locally.
Ascending sensory information is transformed repeatedly before cortex; descending motor commands are likewise shaped by brainstem and spinal circuits.
Autonomic output is anatomically split: sympathetic preganglionic neurons are mainly thoracolumbar; pelvic parasympathetic neurons are sacral.

sources.topic: human spinal cord tracts and Rexed laminae review
